title: Make focused area preservation across bfcache reactivation normative
body:
Follow-up to #5878 and #6696.

## Background

Issue #5878 documented that browsers diverge on focus behavior when a `Document` enters and is restored from the back/forward cache:

- **Safari:** focused element stays focused; no `blur`/`focus` events fire across bfcache.
- **Firefox:** focused element stays focused, but a `blur` fires after `pagehide` and a `focus` fires after `pageshow`.
- **Chrome:** focused element is blurred on entering bfcache and is not refocused on restore.

In #5878 the Mozilla and Google representatives agreed Safari's behavior is preferred (fewer events around bfcache transitions). PR #6696 then added the following non-normative note next to "focused area of the document":

> Even if a document is not fully active and not shown to the user, it can still have a focused area of the document. If a document's fully active state changes, its focused area of the document will stay the same.

WPT https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/31084 exercises this and has been failing on Chromium and Firefox ever since.

## Why open this again

I'm working on Chromium CL https://crrev.com/c/7829940 (bug https://crbug.com/40199280) which aligns Chromium with Safari by preserving the focused element across bfcache. During review on the Chromium side ([comments](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/7829940)) it was pointed out that:

1. The spec text saying focus is preserved is only a note, not normative.
2. Chrome's current "clear focus on bfcache entry" behavior was added very intentionally in https://crrev.com/c/2362046 in 2020, partly to keep IME / text-input plumbing in a clean state.
3. Without a normative spec statement, it's hard to justify the behavior change in Chromium because "the outcome could go either way".

So the request is: please make the focused-area preservation across bfcache normative, so implementations have a clear interop target.

## Proposal

Promote the second sentence of the existing note to normative prose, and (optionally) add an explicit note in the "reactivate a Document" algorithm pointing at it. Concretely something like:

> One focusable area in each `Document` is designated the focused area of the document. [...]
>
> A document's focused area of the document does not change as a side effect of the document's fully active state changing. In particular, neither storing the document in the back/forward cache nor reactivating it from the back/forward cache affects its focused area of the document, and no `focus` or `blur` events are fired as a result of those transitions.

(Drafting a PR alongside this issue.)

## Implementer status

- WebKit: already matches this behavior (shipped).
- Chromium: implementing now in https://crrev.com/c/7829940; blocked on spec clarification.
- Gecko: behavior partially matches (focus preserved) but fires `blur`/`focus` events; would need a follow-up.

## Tests

WPT already exists: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/browsers/browsing-the-web/back-forward-cache/focus.html (from PR web-platform-tests/wpt#31084). Currently passes on Safari, fails on Chromium and Firefox.
